## Praxion vs the classical self-tuner (family used in each run)

Same plant seed, same five frozen disturbance scenarios, post-change MAE (median). *Relay PI nominal* is an Åström–Hägglund relay auto-tune on the nominal machine (rival of Muse v1 frozen). *Relay PI re-tuned* re-identifies with a small-amplitude relay when the SAME degradation detector fires, then redesigns (rival of Full Praxion). Plant seconds are identification time on the machine: for Praxion, the after-change experiments it chose; for the relay, settle + relay. The relay switches in closed loop, which the agent's experiment API does not allow, and its time cap is generous (600 s vs the agent's 160 s), so the comparison leans toward the classical method. Praxion's wall time also includes model latency; the relay's is simulated plant time only.

### Ablation (same plant seed, same frozen scenarios)

Nominal = 10 held-out episodes scored after settling. Post = 5 disturbance episodes, MAE over t >= disturbance time, in-band scored from disturbance + settle. Adaptation latency = median seconds from the disturbance to the start of the FINAL in-band run of the true level, which must last at least 10 s and reach the end of the episode (recovered episodes only); as frozen in `metrics.py` it is 0 s when the level never leaves the band after the change. Overrides and hard violations are shown nominal / post. Model calls and cost: v1 frozen counts calls up to v1's registration; Full Praxion counts the whole run. Wall time: v1 = start to v1 approval; Full = whole run.

### Ablation (same plant seed, same frozen scenarios)

Nominal = 10 held-out episodes scored after settling. Post = 5 disturbance episodes, MAE over t >= disturbance time, in-band scored from disturbance + settle. Adaptation latency = median seconds from the disturbance to the start of the FINAL in-band run of the true level, which must last at least 10 s and reach the end of the episode (recovered episodes only); as frozen in `metrics.py` it is 0 s when the level never leaves the band after the change. Overrides and hard violations are shown nominal / post. Model calls and cost: v1 frozen counts calls up to v1's registration; Full Praxion counts the whole run. Wall time: v1 = start to v1 approval; Full = whole run.

## How to reproduce

```bash
uv sync
uv run python scripts/run_evaluation.py --sandbox docker        # regenerates this file
uv run python scripts/audit_run.py <run_id>                     # independent per-run audit
uv run python scripts/export_artifacts.py <run_id>              # zip bundle for judges
```

- Raw numbers: `artifacts/benchmarks/latest.json`. Fresh reports are cached in `artifacts/benchmarks/cache/<sha256>-<suite>-<plant_seed>.json`; delete that directory to force a full re-score. A cache entry is reused only if the evaluator fingerprint and sandbox mode match.
- Scenario seeds, windows and thresholds are frozen in `backend/evaluation/config.py`; nothing in this report tunes them. The plant seed for each run is read from the trusted audit entries of its stored evaluation report.
- Baselines are transparent and never shown to the model. The *slow PID* tuning was chosen by a small manual sweep on the disturbance scenarios; it is an existence proof that the dynamics disturbance is repairable, not a fair competitor. If a baseline beats Praxion, that is the result.
- The *relay auto-tuned PI* baselines (`backend/evaluation/autotune.py`) are the fair classical rival: a fully automatic relay-feedback identification and Tyreus–Luyben PI design, tuned per plant seed from the same start state the agent discovers from, and re-tuned on the changed machine only when the shared degradation detector fires. Every constant (relay amplitudes, hysteresis, tuning rule) was frozen on exploration seeds 1–20 before any hidden-seed scoring; the per-run notes report plant time used, gains and any hard-cutoff ticks during identification.
